label: r3c2
name: 2 epochs + entropy 0.03
hypothesis: Same as r2c1 (2 PPO epochs, about 231k steps) but ent_coef rises to 0.03. It tests the same anti-collapse fix at an epoch count between the stable 3-epoch r1c2 and the more sample-rich 1-epoch run. Compared with the 1-epoch candidate, it shows which epoch count is best once collapse is controlled. Refuted if a seed collapses to near 0, or if the mean is not above 0.89.
last_analysis: Flipping the head's x-axis is the key fix: placement actions are mirrored in x. Every unflipped network collapsed to choosing DONE at once. Beyond that, the main risk is collapse caused by seed luck. Placements are penalised early in training while DONE scores 0. So 1 epoch (r2c3, r3c1, r3c3) and 2 epochs at entropy 0.01 (r2c1) each lost at least one seed to DONE. Lowering lr made collapse certain. With 2 epochs and entropy 0.03 (r3c2), both seeds survived, giving the best score, 0.936 (0.926/0.945). 3 epochs at entropy 0.01 (r1c2, 0.89) was stable but had fewer samples. The architecture changes so far (both orientations plus depth; stem skip into the head) did worse, partly through slower learning. Dev IoU is about 0.99, so the remaining errors are small. For this final round I make single changes to r3c2: a stronger entropy bonus, 3 epochs with entropy 0.03, and one cheap dilated residual conv for context.
